chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Upon the Sarrorah (the state of Ihram), it is obligatory to shave the head completely and not merely trim (shorten); indeed, trimming is for the one who has performed the Hajj of Islam."

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَام: The first Hajj performed by a person

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shaving and trimming hair when exiting Ihram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the two forms of Tahallul, specifying that complete shaving (Halq) is obligatory for those exiting Ihram due to a specific fault or condition, whereas trimming (Taqsir) is reserved for the standard completion of Hajj al-Ifrad or Hajj al-Qiran. It highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the severity of the expiation (Kaffarah) linked to the method of hair removal, emphasizing that Halq carries a weightier ritual significance than mere trimming.
